notes: Eval 0 (detailed comments plan) is the discriminating case: both configs cover 100% of the actual plan content (character limits, rate limits, Resend/Prisma details, soft-delete permissions, one-level nesting) — a capable model gets the substance right even without the skill. The one point of separation is format fidelity: the baseline used '01-name.md' (no spaces) instead of the skill's specified '01 - name.md', and its REQUIREMENTS.md used different section names ('Summary' instead of 'Overview', no Dependencies section in any feature file). The skill's value here is a predictable, consistent output contract, not better content.

Eval 1 (vague onboarding plan) did not discriminate at all — both with_skill and without_skill runs correctly stopped and asked near-identical clarifying questions instead of fabricating scope, scoring 100% either way. The baseline run's own reasoning cited this repo's AGENTS.md ('Always ask clarifying questions... Never assume design, tech stack or features'), which independently pushes toward the same behavior the skill specifies. This eval mainly confirms the 'don't fabricate scope' behavior holds somewhere in the stack in this repo, but doesn't isolate the skill's unique contribution — worth keeping as a regression guard rather than reading its 0% delta as 'the skill added nothing.'

with_skill runs took modestly longer and used more tokens (+17s, +5096 tokens on average) than baseline, almost entirely driven by eval 0 — the skill's more prescriptive template (Dependencies section per feature, explicit feature index formatting) adds some output volume. This is a reasonable tradeoff for the consistency gained.
